title: Best DevOps Deployment Tools
body:
DevOps deployment tools are all the rage. And for good reason. With this (relatively) new practice, businesses can achieve unheard-of levels of automation. Once your business has reached that new tech nirvana, it will be more agile, more reliable, and capable of delivering faster and more frequently—especially when supported by specialized DevOps services that help implement and maintain these complex toolchains. [...] ## TL;DR

The DevOps toolchain spans CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, containers, monitoring, and security. No single tool covers all of it. The most widely adopted stack in 2025: GitHub Actions (CI/CD), Terraform (IaC), Docker + Kubernetes (containers), Prometheus + Grafana (monitoring), and Datadog or New Relic (APM). The right toolchain matches your team’s maturity and cloud provider. [...] Terraform is an infrastructure-as-code tool that lets you define cloud infrastructure (servers, networks, databases) as code files that are version-controlled and reproducible. Rather than clicking through the AWS console, you write HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) files that provision and manage infrastructure automatically. It’s cloud-agnostic — supporting 1,700+ providers. Most enterprise DevOps teams standardize on it.

title: India trumpets $4.6 billion of investment in home-grown components - Telecoms
body: The Indian government has approved a series of projects that will collectively plough 418.64 billion rupees, or US$4.6 billion, into the manufacture of electronic components under a scheme designed to further the ongoing Made in India initiative. Specifically, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has given the green light to 22 proposals submitted to its Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) last year. "The ECMS seeks to integrate India’s electronic industry with global value chains by encouraging production of essential components, sub-assemblies, and raw materials within the country.". "These approvals will significantly strengthen domestic supply chains, reduce import dependence for critical electronic components, and support the growth of high-value manufacturing capabilities in India," the statement reads. "These approvals under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme reflects a bold, forward-looking step in electronics manufacturing journey, which is closely aligned with the Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of making India a global hub for electronics manufacturing," it concludes.

title: India doubles down on state-backed venture capital, approving $1.1B fund - TechCrunch
body: India has cleared a $1.1 billion state-backed venture capital program that will channel government money into startups through private investors, doubling down on its effort to finance high-risk areas such as artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing and other sectors broadly referred to by the industry as deep tech. It is designed to take a more targeted approach than its 2016 counterpart, focusing on deep-tech and manufacturing startups that typically require longer time horizons and larger amounts of capital, while also backing early-stage founders, expanding investment beyond major cities and strengthening India’s domestic venture capital industry, particularly smaller funds, per the Indian government. The cabinet approval follows recent changes to India’s startup rules aimed at easing pressure on deep-tech companies. The approval comes just ahead of the government-backed India AI Impact Summit, where global AI companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Nvidia are set to participate alongside Indian corporates such as Reliance Industries and Tata Group. The chip delivers 3.2 GHz sustained all-core frequency within a 300W thermal design power envelope, channels over 800 GB/s of [...] What mainstream coverage overwhelmingly gets wrong is the competitive framing. Nearly every headline positions the AGI CPU as a "challenge to Nvidia," driven partly by Arm's stock surging 18% on the announcement. This framing fundamentally misreads the chip's role. The AGI CPU does not compete with Nvidia's H100 or B200 GPUs. It contains no HBM, no tensor cores, no training capability. title: Prime minister of India calls on global semiconductor leaders to support country’s next growth phase - tele.net.in
body: # Prime minister of India calls on global semiconductor leaders to support country’s next growth phase. Prime Minister of India has urged global and domestic semiconductor companies to participate in the next phase of India's semiconductor development, with a focus on scaling manufacturing, strengthening talent and advancing emerging technologies. Addressing a roundtable with semiconductor industry leaders, he highlighted the need for closer collaboration between the government and industry to shape India's technology ecosystem. Referring to the government's target of training one crore people in AI, he said India's talent base, combined with the capabilities and global experience of industry leaders, could create significant opportunities. The prime minister noted that the semiconductor sector has made significant progress and is now moving from its foundational phase towards greater scale and opportunities across the ecosystem. Meanwhile, the participating companies welcomed the government's efforts to build India's semiconductor capabilities and pointed to progress in manufacturing, design, infrastructure and talent development.

title: SEMI Reports Global Semiconductor Equipment Billings Reached $135 Billion in 2025, Up 15% Year-on-Year - The Manila Times
body: # SEMI Reports Global Semiconductor Equipment Billings Reached $135 Billion in 2025, Up 15% Year-on-Year. MILPITAS, Calif., April 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Worldwide sales of semiconductor manufacturing equipment increased 15% to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $117.1 billion in 2024, driven by continued investment in advanced logic, memory, and AI-related capacity expansion, SEMI, the industry association representing the global electronics design and manufacturing supply chain, reported today. "Record semiconductor equipment billings of $135 billion in 2025 underscore the scale and urgency of the industry's buildout as AI accelerates demand for leading-edge logic, advanced memory and high-bandwidth architectures," said Ajit Manocha, SEMI President and CEO. Compiled from data submitted by members of SEMI and the Semiconductor Equipment Association of Japan (SEAJ), the WWSEMS report is a summary of the monthly billings figures for the global semiconductor equipment industry. * Monthly ***Worldwide Semiconductor Equipment Market Statistics******(WWSEMS)****,* a detailed report of semiconductor equipment billings for seven regions and more than 22 market segments.

title: Global semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales projected to reach record $156 billion in 2027, says SEMI - Robotics & Automation News
body: **Global sales of total semiconductor manufacturing equipment by original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) are forecast to reach a record high of $133 billion in 2025, growing 13.7 percent year-on-year, SEMI predicted in its Year-End Total Semiconductor Equipment Forecast – OEM Perspective at SEMICON Japan 2025.**. Growth in semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales is expected to continue in the two following years of the forecast period, with projections of $145 billion in 2026 and $156 billion in 2027. DRAM equipment sales are projected to rise 15.4 percent to $22.5 billion in 2025, followed by 15.1 percent and 7.8 percent year-on-year growth in 2026 and 2027, respectively, as memory suppliers ramp HBM and upgrade to more advanced process nodes to meet AI and data center requirements. In Taiwan, robust 2025 spending reflects large-scale leading-edge capacity builds for AI and high-performance computing, while Korea’s equipment outlays are supported by substantial investments in advanced memory technologies, including HBM.

title: Global Semiconductor Equipment Sales Projected to Reach a Record of $156 Billion in 2027, SEMI Reports - The Manila Times
body: Global Semiconductor Equipment Sales Projected to Reach a Record of $156 Billion in 2027, SEMI Reports. TOKYO, Dec. 16, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Global sales of total semiconductor manufacturing equipment by original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) are forecast to reach a record high of $133 billion in 2025, growing 13.7% year-on-year, SEMI announced today in its *Year-End Total Semiconductor Equipment Forecast - OEM Perspective* at SEMICON Japan 2025. Growth in semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales is expected to continue in the two following years of the forecast period, with projections of $145 billion in 2026 and $156 billion in 2027. "Global semiconductor equipment sales show robust momentum, with both the front-end and back-end segments projected to see three consecutive years of growth, culminating in total sales surpassing $150 billion for the first time in 2027," said Ajit Manocha, SEMI president and CEO.

title: Govt plans RMG-style incentive to spur semiconductor industry growth - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
body: DHAKA, Aug 06, 2026 (BSS)-  Aimed at accelerating development of semiconductor industry in the country the government is mulling introduce incentive facilities for this sector similar to ready-made garments (RMG). Talking to BSS, Managing Director of the Bangladesh Hi-Tech Park Authority (BHTPA) Fazlur Rahman said the government has designated the semiconductor sector as a strategic one and tasked the authorities for its development through supportive policies and investment promotion. The government seeks to make position for Bangladesh as a competitive player in the global chip value chain, he added. Fazlur Rahman, however, described that the government's broader strategy aims to establish a comprehensive semiconductor ecosystem encompassing chip design, testing, packaging and advanced manufacturing through fiscal incentives, research, skill development, international collaboration and investment promotion. Managing Director of the iTest Bangladesh Limited Munir Ahmed said Bangladesh has the potential to become a competitive player in the global semiconductor market by initially focusing on chip design and semiconductor testing before expanding into OSAT activities.

### Agentic editing

Composer 2.5 is the main multi-file feature here. You describe a task in natural language, and it plans and applies changes across several files in one pass. There’s also a built-in diff review, so you can accept or reject changes one file at a time. [...] Claude Code uses sub-agents that plan, code, review, and test, so it can handle multi-step work across files and branches. That’s the big idea here: instead of just suggesting code, it can work through a chain of tasks with less hand-holding.

In June 2026, with sub-agents enabled, it completed a full feature build in a 200,000-line TypeScript project in 9 minutes. That work included an API endpoint, a migration, a service layer, and docs. [...] ### Repo context

title: AI Agent Company Decagon Held Early M&A Talks With ServiceNow, Others - Business Insider
body: Buzzy AI agent startup Decagon could be the latest company swept up in a growing wave of AI dealmaking. The company, which was last valued at $4.5 billion earlier this year, has hired a bank to evaluate acquisition interest, according to people familiar with the matter. The interest in Decagon represents a new shift in the AI boom: after years of huge venture rounds and soaring valuations, tech companies are increasingly looking to buy their way into promising AI markets. Growing AI-related businesses are often getting offers at a significant premium to their last valuation, so if Decagon were to accept an offer, it could be considerably higher than its previous $4.5 billion value. It competes with industry veteran Bret Taylor's Sierra, which was valued at $15.8 billion earlier this year. It was also punished for making a $7 billion acquisition of the security business Armis, a deal announced late last year.

title: Skild AI worth $14B, Airwallex's Series G, and BioMatrix makes a buy. - Axios
body: • **Skild AI**, a Pittsburgh-based AI robotics company, is in talks to raise more than $1b in Series C funding at an approximately $14b valuation from **SoftBank** and **Nvidia**, per Reuters. • **Airwallex**, an Australia-based payments firm, raised US$330m in Series G funding at an $8b valuation. • **Resemble AI**, a deepfakes detection startup, raised $13m from Google's AI Future Fund, Okta Ventures, Taiwania Capital, Gentree Fund, IAG Capital Partners, Berkeley Frontier Fund, and KDDI. • **Rotostitch**, an SF-based textile manufacturing tech startup, raised $1m in pre-seed funding led by **Boost VC** and **Nova Threshold**. • **Harbor IT,** a Brazilian managed IT services provider, acquired **ZAG Technical Services**, a San Jose, Calif.-based cybersecurity services company. • **Millman**, a Seattle-based consulting firm, acquired **MorVest Capital**, a Port O'Connor, Texas-based mortgage servicing rights analytics company. • **Andersen Group**, an SF-based tax advisory formed by former Arthur Andersen partners, set IPO terms to 11m shares at $14-$16.
